verdict.rationale: Glama's docs show it functions as an MCP directory/gateway/hosting layer: users can search and connect to thousands of servers, get pre-filled config blocks for clients, and route all MCP calls through Glama's Gateway which sits in front of any deployed server (glama-docs-4, glama-docs-11, glama-docs-13, glama-docs-14, glama-docs-15, glama-docs-6). This supports plugging in MCP servers so tools flow through the product, but the evidence centers on hosting/proxying infrastructure rather than Glama's own chat/agent directly invoking tools end-to-end, and community reports note friction (undocumented billing gating rebuilds) that complicates the pipeline. Missing for 10: first-party or hands-on evidence that Glama's own chat/agent interface actually calls and uses tools from a connected server, and independent confirmation the gateway experience works smoothly in practice.
